questions_and_answers.question: The compound interest on Rs.30000 at 7% per annum is Rs.4347. The period is a. 4 years b. 3 years c. 2.5 years d. 2 years
questions_and_answers.answer: d. 2 years. The question asks for the period of time for which a principal amount of Rs. 30000 will accumulate a compound interest of Rs. 4347 at an annual interest rate of 7%. To solve this, we can use the compound interest formula: A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) Where: * A is the amount after time t * P is the principal amount * r is the annual interest rate * n is the number of times that interest is compounded per year * t is the time in years In this case, we are given: * P = Rs. 30000 * r = 7% = 0.07 * A = P + compound interest = Rs. 30000 + Rs. 4347 = Rs. 34347 We need to find t. Assuming the interest is compounded annually (n = 1), we can plug the values into the formula and solve for t: 34347 = 30000(1 + 0.07/1)^(1*t) 34347/30000 = (1.07)^t 1.1449 = (1.07)^t To solve for t, we can use logarithms: log(1.1449) = t * log(1.07) t = log(1.1449) / log(1.07) t ≈ 2 Therefore, the period is approximately 2 years.
